rationale: CL-P0-008 gap-to-B=1 eligible predict build (fifth of the mechanism, third engine family: sequenceBuild after triangleSolve and shuffleTest). Authored a predict on the causal step i1 (sequenceBuild geometric dial, manip=2/conseq=2): the dial starts at r=0.9, and the prediction asks whether the forever-sum's ceiling there sits above or below the 8 target before the learner touches it. Outcome above (4/(1-0.9)=40, the widget's own start readout), against the genuine misconception that shrinking terms alone keep the pile small; the reveal asserts only what the widget already shows (ceiling 40) and what highFeedback already claims (terms shrink too slowly, ceiling escapes as r approaches 1), and never states the r=0.5 answer. Verified: Lesson.safeParse VALID, lintLesson clean, evaluate at dial 9/5/3 routes to high/success/low as predicted, cml-lint 0 errors, tier recompute (non-writing scratchpad copy) confirms prediction 0->3, total 23->26, tier C->B and no other dimension moved.
reopenCondition: Reopen if step i1's widget numbers (first, start, targetRTenths, targetSum) change without re-deriving the predict's above/below outcome from the new start ratio.

rationale: CL-P0-008 gap-to-B=1 eligible predict build (fourth engine family: ciCapture). Both interactive steps qualify on capabilities (i1 and i1b, ciCapture manip=2/conseq=2); i1b was deliberately rejected as the landing site because concept c2 immediately before it states outright that raising the level widens the interval, which would make any wider-or-narrower prediction there forced. Built on i1 instead: before drawing any bars, predict how often a bar at the 80% width will miss the dashed truth line (1 in 5 vs 1 in 20 vs almost never). Outcome 1-in-5 requires reading the level as the method's long-run capture rate, the lesson's target invariant, and is stated nowhere before i1; the reveal asserts only what i1's own wrongLevelFeedback already claims (80% misses about 1 time in 5; 99% almost never misses but says little). Verified: Lesson.safeParse VALID, lintLesson clean, evaluate routes level-80 to wrongLevelFeedback and level-95/20-drawn to success, cml-lint 0 errors, tier recompute (non-writing scratchpad copy) confirms prediction 0->3, total 23->26, tier C->B.
reopenCondition: Reopen if step i1's levels, targetLevel, or its wrongLevelFeedback's 1-in-5 claim change without re-deriving the predict's outcome and reveal.

rationale: CL-P0-008 gap-to-B=1 eligible predict build (fifth engine family: circleMeasureExplore arcSector). The obvious what-will-the-arc-read question was rejected as forced: concept c2 immediately before i2 computes the exact answer (radius 4, 90 degrees, s = 2pi ~ 6.28) while teaching the degrees-in-rtheta wreck. Built instead on the one directional fact c2 does NOT state: opening the angle from the 20-degree start to 90 degrees is 4.5x the turn, and the prediction asks whether the arc also comes out exactly 4.5x as long, or grows slower (the chord/straight-line intuition) or faster. Outcome exactly-4.5x is the strict proportionality that i2's own successFeedback asserts ('the arc is just the fraction of a lap the angle sweeps'); the reveal cites only the widget's own displayed readouts (about 1.4 at 20 degrees, 2pi ~ 6.28 at 90) and that existing feedback sentence. Verified: Lesson.safeParse VALID, lintLesson clean, evaluate at 90/45/120 routes to success/low/high, arc(90)/arc(20) === 4.5 exactly and the cited rounded readouts match the widget's fmt, cml-lint 0 errors, tier recompute (non-writing scratchpad copy) confirms prediction 0->3, total 23->26, tier C->B.
reopenCondition: Reopen if step i2's radius, start angle, or targetAngle change without re-deriving the 4.5x factor and the reveal's cited readouts.
